summary: Australian reviewers regard the updated Model 3 as the class benchmark among electric sedans, praising a noticeably quieter cabin and softer ride than earlier versions alongside brisk performance and strong efficiency. The Long Range RWD's 750km WLTP claim makes it the longest-range EV sold in the country, while the screen-only control layout continues to split opinion. The Performance variant's near-$81,000 list price also pushes it close to the FBT exemption threshold that keeps novated-lease buyers interested in the cheaper variants.
pros: Long Range RWD offers the longest WLTP range of any EV on sale in Australia at 750km
Access to Tesla's extensive Australian Supercharger network plus regular over-the-air software updates
Recent refresh brings a quieter cabin and noticeably improved ride comfort over the outgoing model
Strong outright performance, with the dual-motor Performance variant hitting 100km/h in around 3.1 seconds
cons: Touchscreen-only interface, including indicators and gear selection on some builds, remains a sticking point for reviewers
Comprehensive insurance premiums tend to sit at the higher end of the EV market due to repair and parts costs
Performance variant's list price sits close to the $75,000 FBT exemption threshold, eroding some of the novated-lease tax advantage
